title: How to Fish
genre: Online co-op physics fishing / comedic shooter ('friendslop'), 1-4 players (lobbies up to 8 since patch 1.0.4)
release_date: 2026-08-20 (Steam, PC; full release, not Early Access)
window_note: in window (released 2026-08-20). THE BENCHMARK game for this study.
developer: Dazed Games (Skövde/Gothenburg, Sweden). Founders: Carl-Vilhelm Johansson and Melvin Olsson
team_size: 2 [CONFIRMED – Sweden Game Arena profile; the 1M Steam news post is signed by both founders; press calls the studio 'literally two people']
developer_background: Founders met studying game development at LBS High School in Gothenburg. Their first game, 'Out of Hand' (student project; 'Out of Hand: Deluxe' released free on Steam), went viral in China after a Chinese YouTuber video and reached ~180,000–200,000 players [CONFIRMED – Sweden Game Arena]. A paid online version launched in summer 2025 sold 'significantly lower than hoped'; Olsson says 'we weren't good at marketing'. They abandoned it and started How to Fish in August 2025. Joined Science Park Skövde's 'Sweden Game Startup' program ('We knew how to make a game, but we had no idea how to start a company or make money from it'). Met Landfall via Science Park Skövde and signed a project investment about a week after a Berlin trade fair.
publisher: Self-published on Steam (Steam lists Dazed Games as developer AND publisher) with project-based investment from Evil Landfall, the investment/publishing arm of Landfall Games (PEAK, Content Warning). Landfall took no equity in the studio; the investment covers the game only. Some outlets (CBR, TechTimes) describe Evil Landfall as publisher/backer.
platforms_and_store_links: Steam (PC, Steam Deck Verified): https://store.steampowered.com/app/4001890/How_to_Fish/ ; Consoles (PS5/Xbox) and Mac: planned, no date [CONFIRMED – dev FAQ/Olsson quote via Insider Gaming, Push Square, GamesRadar]
business_model: Premium, $7.99 list with 38% launch discount to $4.95 until 2026-08-27. Free content updates (v1.1.0 'Islet Update' 2026-09-28). A How to Fish + PEAK Steam bundle was added with v1.1.0. No DLC/MTX reported.
price_usd: $7.99 list; $4.95 launch price (-38%) 2026-08-20 to 2026-08-27 [CONFIRMED – Steam store / GamesRadar]
units_or_downloads: 1,000,000 copies by 2026-08-22, i.e. ~48 h after launch [CONFIRMED – dev Steam news post '1 MILLION FISHERMEN IN 2 DAYS', via GamesRadar, Sweden Game Arena, Dot Esports]. >6.3M units by end of Aug 2026 [ESTIMATE – GameDiscoverCo Aug-2026 report]. >8.5M units lifetime by end of Sep 2026 [ESTIMATE – GameDiscoverCo Sep-2026 report, Steam only, excludes keys]. Boxleiter cross-check: ~69,000 all-language reviews (late Sep 2026 snapshot) × 80 (implied ratio at the 1M milestone) ≈ 5.5M; × 120 ≈ 8.3M [ESTIMATE]. Steam Page Analyzer's low-multiplier model gives only ~593k (395k–791k), which the confirmed 1M already exceeds, so disregard it. Dev target had been ~200,000 copies [CONFIRMED – Olsson via Sweden Game Arena]. No dev-announced milestone beyond 1M found as of 2026-10-08.
peak_concurrent_players: All-time peak 373,971 on ~2026-08-25/26 [CONFIRMED – SteamDB via GamesRadar and DLCompare; SteamCharts shows 373,887, Raijin 372,634]. Timeline: 22,076 within 24 h of launch (SteamDB via Dexerto); 170,759 earlier high; 268,101 on 2026-08-23; 341,691 on 2026-08-24 (SteamDB post on X). Post-peak, a later undated snapshot shows ~27,000 concurrent with a 24-h peak ~59,500 (DLCompare). Twitch: TheBurntPeanut was the top channel in week 1 with 330,829 hours watched [ESTIMATE – Streams Charts].
steam_reviews: ~12,000–13,000 reviews (~94% positive) on ~2026-08-22/23 (Techlomedia 'nearly 12,000'; brief ~13k). 61,145 all-language, 95.1% positive on 2026-09-12 (review roundup citing Steam). 68,344–69,053 all-language, 95% positive at the latest indexed snapshot (Raijin; Steam store Norwegian capture; late Sep / early Oct 2026). English-only: 27,213, 95% 'Overwhelmingly Positive'; last 30 days 20,261, 94% 'Very Positive'. Exact count on 2026-10-08: no data (likely ~70k+).
implied_review_multiplier: ~77–83 at the 1M milestone (1,000,000 CONFIRMED units ÷ ~12,000–13,000 reviews on 2026-08-22/23). Use ~80 as the calibration point for cheap viral friendslop. If GameDiscoverCo's >8.5M (end Sep) is right, the ratio vs ~69k reviews is ~120+. That is an estimate on an estimate, but it suggests the ratio grows after the launch spike.
gross_revenue: >$38M lifetime Steam gross through Sep 2026 [ESTIMATE – GameDiscoverCo Sep-2026 report]. GDCo August chart: ~$26M gross in Aug 2026, #2 new Steam release by revenue [ESTIMATE – GameDiscoverCo]. Spec method cross-check: 8.5M × ($7.99 × 0.75 = $5.99) ≈ $51M. That overstates the total because most units (≥6.3M of 8.5M) sold during the $4.95 launch week or under regional pricing. GDCo's figure implies ~$4.47 per unit, which is consistent with that. Chosen central value ≈ $38M (range $32M–$51M).
net_revenue: ≈ $26M [ESTIMATE] = $38M gross − Steam cut (30% on first $10M = $3.0M; 25% on next $28M = $7.0M) = $28.0M × 0.93 (refunds/chargebacks) ≈ $26.0M to Dazed Games + Evil Landfall combined. The revenue split with Evil Landfall is undisclosed. Swedish corporate tax is not deducted.
production_cost: ≈ $144k [ESTIMATE – 2 people × 12 months × $6k/month, W. Europe lean indie]. Evil Landfall's project investment amount is undisclosed; the label is reported to offer up to ~$1M per project. No paid marketing budget reported.
development_time: ~12 months, Aug 2025 → Aug 2026 [CONFIRMED – founders via Sweden Game Arena: 'in August last year they started working on…How to Fish'; 'after a year of development']
why_popular: Simple, instantly readable hook: a calm fishing game that turns into chaos. You catch absurd sea creatures, then shoot or blow them up with SMGs, dynamite and brass knuckles; gamble your catch; fight seagulls and boss fish; sell the catch and upgrade your boat. It has physics-comedy moments built for clips, a 1–4 friend co-op 'friendslop' format (PEAK/R.E.P.O./Lethal Company lineage) and an impulse price ($4.95 launch, so friends buy 4-packs). Reviewed as 'perfect for killing time'. The Landfall/PEAK halo gave it credibility. Launched in late-summer school holidays.
marketing_channels: Weekly short-form feature videos on TikTok/Instagram (@dazed_games) for months before launch: several million views and a 1,300-member Discord by the time of the Landfall pitch; individual TikToks reached ~84k likes [CONFIRMED – Sweden Game Arena; TikTok]. Landfall's own channels promoted the launch ('How To Fish by Dazed Games is out!' on Landfall TikTok) and a PEAK bundle followed. Launch-week streamer and YouTube 'friendslop' wave: TheBurntPeanut was the top Twitch channel (330k hours watched in week 1), plus many small group streams. Steep 38% launch discount. Press snowball from the SteamDB CCU posts ('Steam lottery winner'). No public demo/playtest (site FAQ: 'no playtesters, sorry'). Next Fest participation: no data. Pre-launch wishlists: no data.
engine: Unity (Unity 6, build 6000.4.4f1) [ESTIMATE – Unity version string in a player's crash report on the Steam discussions; PlayTracker lists the game as a Unity game; no dev statement found]
art_style: Stylised, low-fi first-person 3D with physics-driven comedy; bright ocean/islands; cartoonish creatures
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write most gameplay and netcode boilerplate (Claude Code with Unity + Netcode for GameObjects/Fishnet/Photon Fusion, or Godot 4 + GodotSteam), generate low-poly creatures, boats and props (Meshy/Tripo), produce SFX (ElevenLabs), music (Suno/Udio), UI text and the Steam page copy. | AI cannot: make physics-based co-op feel good and in sync (boat, ragdoll and fish physics under latency is the hard part), tune the comedic chaos and economy loop, run many group playtests, or reproduce the 9+ months of consistent TikTok devlog marketing and the Landfall relationship. The 2-person team took 12 months. | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity 6 (or Godot 4) + Steamworks lobbies/relay (Facepunch.Steamworks / GodotSteam) + Meshy/Tripo + Blender cleanup + ElevenLabs SFX + Suno music + CapCut for TikTok clips.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 6–10 weeks, ~$300–$900 (Claude Max $100–$200/mo × 2–3 months, 3D gen $30–$60/mo, audio $10–$30/mo, asset packs $50–$200, Steam Direct $100). Excludes the developer's living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 6–10 months, ~$3,000–$12,000 (tools ~$250/mo, asset packs $300–$800, freelance polish for animation/trailer/key art $1,000–$5,000, playtest and creator outreach $500–$2,000, Steam $100). Excludes living costs. The market outcome depends heavily on months of short-form video marketing.

data_conflicts: (1) Publisher: the brief says self-published, and Steam lists Dazed Games as publisher, but CBR/TechTimes say it was 'published with support from' or 'bankrolled by' Evil Landfall. Chosen: self-published with Evil Landfall project investment and no equity. (2) All-time peak: 373,971 (SteamDB per GamesRadar/DLCompare, dated Aug 25 '5 days after launch' vs Aug 26) vs 373,887 (SteamCharts) vs 372,634 (Raijin). Chosen 373,971 on ~Aug 25–26. (3) Date of the 1M announcement: Aug 22 (most outlets) vs '3 days after launch' (TURGAME). Chosen Aug 22. (4) Reviews at 1M: 'nearly 12,000' (Techlomedia) vs ~13k (brief), so the implied ratio is a range of 77–83. (5) GameDiscoverCo: Aug gross $26M + Sep gross $6.5M = $32.5M, which does not reconcile with the stated '>$38M LTD'. That could be a revision or different cut-off dates. Reported both and chose $38M as the latest. (6) Player count: the store says 1–4 players, while the wiki/patch notes say lobbies of up to 8 since 1.0.4. (7) Release plan: an April 2026 article said 'end of 2026' and the site said Q3 2026; the actual release was Aug 20. (8) Steam Page Analyzer's ~593k estimate is inconsistent with the confirmed 1M and was rejected.
notes: Post-launch: patches 1.0.4 (lobby limit 4→8), 1.0.5 (private invite-only lobbies), 1.0.12 on 2026-09-04 (Steam Cloud saves, last bug-fix-only patch), v1.1.0 'Islet Update' on 2026-09-28 (mini islands, Manta mini-boss, bow weapon, new bait/creatures/NPC/outfit/achievements, PEAK bundle), then 1.1.2/1.1.3 on 2026-09-29. Takeaways for a solo creator: (a) the first game failed commercially but taught the team marketing; (b) the publisher-light model (project investment, keep IP) can still bring a big label's halo; (c) months of weekly TikTok feature clips built the audience before launch; (d) a sub-$5 launch price plus co-op multi-pack buying produced roughly 80 units per review at the start, rising later. RELATED PRECEDENTS: WEBFISHING (Steam 2024-10-11, $4.99; developer and publisher 'lamedeveloper' (one person, per Steam listing); a remake of an 8-day 2022 itch.io game-jam project; cosy social fishing chatroom). Reviews: ~70,252, 97% positive (Raijin, 2026-07-22) / 69,258, ~97.5% (Vaporlens); just under 5,000 reviews, 98% positive, in launch week (Inverse). All-time peak CCU 23,838 (Tracker.gg). Sales are unconfirmed by the dev, and tracker estimates disagree widely: ~1.3M copies / ~$5.6M gross (Raijin, 2026-07-22, medium confidence); 1–2M owners (SteamSpy); ~5.06M / ~$25.2M (Vaporlens) [all ESTIMATE]. Engine (Godot) is unverified; it was not confirmed in this session's searches. Sources: https://raijin.gg/app/3146520/WEBFISHING , https://steamspy.com/dev/lamedeveloper , https://tracker.gg/population/steam/3146520 , https://www.inverse.com/gaming/steam-webfishing-cozy-chatroom-game-animal-crossing . It is the direct ancestor of the social-fishing hook, but How to Fish's peak CCU was ~16× higher. Fisch (Roblox, 2024) and Cast n Chill (2025, cosy idle fishing in a small desktop window): unverified, from memory only. Fisch shows fishing progression loops can scale to Roblox's young audience; Cast n Chill shows the 'desktop companion' idle-fishing niche. How to Fish combines the social fishing of WEBFISHING with PEAK-style physics-comedy co-op and shooter chaos.
